title: Everton reach Folarin Balogun agreement with Monaco
author: Patrick Boyland
content:
Everton have reached an agreement with Monaco for the signing of U.S. men’s national team striker Folarin Balogun.

Monaco sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, stated a deal consisting of an initial €45million (£38.58m; $52.3m) plus €5million (£4.3m; $5.8m) in potential add-ons had been agreed between the two clubs, while Everton sources said the deal was worth in the region of £40million ($54m; €46.7m).

Personal terms for the 25-year-old are still in the process of being finalised.

The Athletic reported on Monday that Everton were in preliminary talks with Monaco over a move for Balogun, who has two years remaining on his existing contract with the Ligue 1 club.

Balogun was expected to leave Monaco this summer, with talks having not taken place over an extension of his terms.

Everton have been in the market for a striker ahead of Tuesday’s deadline, with Beto nearing a move to Fiorentina, having undergone a medical on Monday. Beto’s departure would leave Everton with one recognised striker in Thierno Barry.

After an injury-disrupted 2024-25 campaign, Balogun returned 19 goals and five assists in 43 appearances for Monaco last season, his best return since joining the club from Arsenal in 2023, in a deal worth an initial €30million, with a further €10m in add-ons (£34.5m; $45.6m at current exchange rates).

Balogun had an impressive World Cup on home soil this summer, scoring three times in four appearances, finishing at the USMNT’s top scorer in their run to the round of 16.

After being sent off in his side’s round of 32 win over Bosnia & Herzegovina, Balogun’s standard one-game ban was suspended by FIFA, which followed a call from President Donald Trump to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, with the decision drawing widespread criticism. He subsequently featured in the round of 16 match against Belgium, which the U.S. lost 4-1.

Balogun progressed through Arsenal’s academy and made 10 first-team appearances for the north London club. The striker enjoyed his breakout season on loan at Ligue 1 club Reims in the 2022-23 campaign, scoring 22 times in 39 appearances, before his move to Monaco.

Analysis from senior soccer writer Tom Bogert

The USMNT breakout star at the World Cup is set to have a new club and he’s heading back to England.

On the field, a return to England suits Balogun’s game. His verticality and intelligence of movement opens space in the attack while he’s physical enough to deal with the rigours of the Premier League.

Balogun will need to finish chances at a high rate because David Moyes teams don’t always provide for centre forwards. Everton haven’t had a double-digit goal scorer in the league since 2021-22. They haven’t had a 15-goal scorer since 2020-21. They have had one 20-goal scorer this century (Romelu Lukaku, 2016-17).

Off the field, a move to the Premier League will continue his star rise in America. Fans of the national team were long aware of his abilities but to a more casual audience, Balogun introduced himself at the World Cup. While he’s swapping the Champions League for the Premier League, not many Americans tune into Ligue 1 regularly. They do watch the Premier League in droves, though.

Balogun was expected to move this summer after indicating he wouldn’t sign a new contract at Monaco. The Ligue 1 side had a high asking price and left it late but, eventually, a deal is close.

Analysis from Everton correspondent Patrick Boyland

Should he agree personal terms and sign for Everton before Tuesday’s deadline, Balogun would be following former USMNT stars Brian McBride, Tim Howard and Landon Donovan in representing the Merseyside club.

Everton have a rich history in the English game. They are one of the Premier League’s ever-presents and were last relegated from the top-flight in the 1950-51 season. They have won the English title nine times. But their last success came when they won the 1995 FA Cup and the club’s passionate fans long for a return to the glory days.

Everton were bought by Houston-based The Friedkin Group in December 2024, ending years of financial strife. They left Goodison Park, their home of 133 years, at the end of the 2024-25 season, and now play games at the neat 53,000 capacity Hill Dickinson Stadium, on Liverpool’s waterfront. The impressive facility, which will host games at the 2028 European Championship, was designed by American architect Dan Meis.

One of the league’s best stadiums, it would be a fitting arena for someone like Balogun to ply his trade.

A replacement for Beto, he will be tasked with adding more finishing quality to an at times goal-shy attack and propelling Everton towards European qualification and/or silverware.
